title: Plant a seed together and take turns keeping it alive
description: One pot, one seed, two or more caretakers. A shared plant turns looking after something into a small team project — with a rota, a windowsill, and a green reward.

body.heading: Start together
paragraphs: Choose a fast, forgiving seed: beans, sunflowers, or cress all sprout quickly enough to hold anyone's interest. Fill a pot with compost together, press the seed in about a fingertip deep, water it, and give the pot a name and the sunniest windowsill you have.
Write the names of the caretakers on a card and stick it in the soil. This plant has a team, and the card is its team sheet.

body.heading: Share the care
paragraphs: Make a simple rota: one person waters on Mondays and Thursdays, another checks the soil on other days and turns the pot a quarter-turn so it grows straight instead of leaning toward the light. Anyone who spots the first shoot gets to announce it, loudly, to the whole household.
Keep a tiny diary beside the pot — a line or a sketch every few days. Shared attention is the real crop here; the bean is almost a bonus.

body.heading: Harvest, whatever it is
paragraphs: If the plant thrives, celebrate the first flower or bean together and cook or display it like a trophy. If it struggles, troubleshoot as a team — more light? less water? — and plant again without blame.
Either way you will have practised the skill underneath every shared project: noticing something small, regularly, together, and caring what happens next.

takeaway: One seed, a named pot and a watering rota turn plant care into teamwork — and shared attention is the real harvest.
materials: A pot with drainage holes and a saucer
A card and pencil for the team sheet and diary
supervision: An adult helps younger gardeners with compost and watering, and chooses a safe, stable spot for the pot.
safetyNotes: Wash hands after handling compost and soil.
Keep seeds away from babies and toddlers, who may put them in their mouths.
Place the pot where it cannot be knocked off a sill onto anyone below.
